figures.finding: Indonesia's Manpower Act forbids employers to employ children (anyone under eighteen), save light work from thirteen to fifteen (with parents' written permission, a work agreement with them, at most three hours a day in daytime outside school), work from fourteen within school curricula, and work to develop a child's talents and interests; the Act names no general age at which employment opens below eighteen beyond these exceptions (layer 3's blocker was the source, now read in the Ministry's translation).

value.talentWork: any age, under the Ministerial Decision

figures.applies: Act 13 of 2003 arts. 1(26), 68-71, Ministry of Manpower's English translation (later amendments by the Job Creation law, UU 6/2023, not read for these articles).

sources.said: 26. A child is every person who is under 18 (eighteen) years ... Entrepreneurs are not allowed to employ children. ... (1) Exemption from what is stipulated under Article 68 may made for the employment of children aged between 13 (thirteen) years old and 15 (fifteen) years old for light work to the extent that the job does not stunt or disrupt their physical, mental and social developments. ... a. The entrepreneurs must have written permission from the parents or guardians of the children; b. There must be a work agreement between the entrepreneur and the parents or guardians; c. Maximum working time 3 (three) hours a day; ... (2) The children as mentioned under subsection (1) at least 14 (fourteen) years of age.

figures.finding: A child may work to develop talent and interest (bakat dan minat: work usually done from early age, that the child likes, within his ability, fostering creativity), always under a parent's or guardian's direct supervision; an employer of a child under fifteen must make a written work agreement with the parent or guardian representing the child, keep work outside school hours, at most three hours a day and twelve a week, have the parent on site, keep the place free of narcotics, gambling, alcohol and prostitution, give a rest place while waiting (waiting over an hour counts as work), and report on the prescribed form to the district labour office at least fourteen days before the child starts. No lowest age is set. The rule is framed around the child's talent and interest (reading: it reaches a child actor and could reach a child writing or directing).

value.report: form to the district (kabupaten/kota) labour office, 14 days before

figures.applies: Act 13 of 2003 art. 71; Kepmenakertrans KEP.115/MEN/VII/2004 arts. 1-6.

sources.said: (1) Children may work in order to develop their talents and interest. (2) Entrepreneurs who employ children as mentioned under subsection (1) are under an obligation to meet the following requirements: a. put under direct supervision of their parents or guardians; b. maximum working time 3 (three) hours a day;

(1) Anak dapat melakukan pekerjaan untuk mengembangkan bakat dan minatnya. ... (1) Pengusaha dilarang mempekerjakan anak untuk mengembangkan bakat dan minat tanpa pengawasan langsung orang tua/wali. ... (1) Pengusaha yang mempekerjakan anak yang berumur kurang dari 15 (lima belas) tahun untuk mengembangkan bakat dan minat, wajib: a. membuat perjanjian kerja secara tertulis dengan orang tua/wali yang mewakili anak dan memuat kondisi dan syarat kerja sesuai dengan ketentuan yang berlaku; b. mempekerjakan di luar waktu sekolah; c. memenuhi ketentuan waktu kerja paling lama 3 (tiga) jam sehari dan 12 (dua belas) jam seminggu; d. melibatkan orang tua/wali di lokasi tempat kerja untuk melakukan pengawasan langsung; ... (3) Laporan sebagaimana dimaksud dalam ayat (2) disampaikan paling lambat 14 (empat belas) hari sebelum pengusaha mempekerjakan anak.

figures.finding: A child's work contract in Indonesia is made between the employer and the child's parent or guardian: for light work (13 to 15) a work agreement with the parents and their written permission, and for talent work under fifteen a written agreement with the parent or guardian who represents the child. No set-aside of earnings was found.

value.binding: written agreement with the parent or guardian (Act 13/2003 art. 69; KEP.115/2004 art. 5)

sources.said: a. membuat perjanjian kerja secara tertulis dengan orang tua/wali yang mewakili anak dan memuat kondisi dan syarat kerja sesuai dengan ketentuan yang berlaku;

figures.finding: Indonesia has two readings of the age of majority, unsettled: the Civil Code (KUHPerdata art. 330) makes a minor anyone under twenty-one who has not married, while the Marriage Law (UU 1/1974 art. 47) keeps a child under eighteen in the parents' power and the Supreme Court's circular SEMA 7/2012 takes eighteen as the age of legal capacity; the Supreme Court has set art. 330 aside (No. 1865 K/PDT/2019) but lower courts still apply it. Both readings are recorded; eighteen is the later rule.
figures.applies: Indonesia (the statutes' own texts not reached: peraturan.bpk.go.id 403, peraturan.go.id did not connect).

figures.finding: An Indonesian limited company's (PT) director must be a natural person capable of legal acts (UU 40/2007 art. 93(1)), with no age of its own, so the director's age follows the age of majority, itself read as twenty-one (KUHPerdata art. 330) or eighteen (the Marriage Law and the Supreme Court's circular); a young producer's company can be directed from eighteen only on the second reading.

value.director: natural person capable of legal acts
barred: director of a company made bankrupt within 5 years
convicted of a financial crime within 5 years
